feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence from earlier races: iteration 4 (404.6, best) gave 20 of 20 oval finishes and s-bend progress 0.486 at wheel_radius 0.035 m and wheel_track 0.09 m. Iteration 1 (337.6) showed that wheel_track 0.10 m alone, at y=0.07 m, left s-bend progress at 0.236, against 0.446 at 0.09 m (iteration 3). So the track width matters for the s-bend independently of the radius-to-track ratio, and the ratio argument is not yet proven. The slalom has stayed at progress 0.16 to 0.18 across iterations 1, 3, 4 and 5 whatever the track, row position or footprint, which points to speed or lag, not sensing. Iteration 6 showed that a 0.016 m footprint collapsed the oval, and iteration 2 showed a wider array raised oscillation, so sensing stays fixed. Depending on the next race: if the s-bend holds at 0.45 or above and the oval keeps 18 or more finishes, keep radius 0.040 m and try lower mass for acceleration. If the s-bend falls below about 0.4 with track 0.10 m, the track is the cause, so return it to 0.09 m. If the oval finishes fall below 17 or oscillation exceeds about 0.3, return radius to 0.035 m, as the speed gain is then costing stability.
requested_changes: If s-bend progress falls below about 0.4 with wheel_track 0.10 m (iteration 1 gave 0.236 at 0.10 m versus 0.446 at 0.09 m in iteration 3), keep wheel_radius 0.040 m but set wheel_track to 0.09 m, which separates the speed effect from the track effect.

If the slalom stays at 0.17 to 0.18 progress with max_error near 0.06 (iterations 1, 3, 4 and 5), try mass 0.5 kg at wheel_radius 0.040 m, since acceleration is untested and sensing and track changes have not moved the slalom.
If oval finishes fall below 17 of 20 or steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.3, return wheel_radius to 0.035 m and wheel_track to 0.09 m, the iteration 4 values that gave 20 of 20 oval finishes.
